chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no objection to As-Salam (forward payment for goods) in merchandise when you describe the length and width."

key_terms.السَّلَمِ: Salam (a forward sale where payment is made in advance for goods to be delivered later)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid Salam contract in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), affirming the validity of the Salam contract for movable goods (matā'ī) when essential attributes like length and width are specified to eliminate gharar (uncertainty). This ruling reflects the practical needs of early Shia communities for forward financing in trade, distinguishing it from the more restrictive views on Salam for non-standardized commodities found in other schools of jurisprudence.
